question: A healthy 22-year-old male participates in a research study you are leading to compare the properties of skeletal and cardiac muscle. You conduct a 3-phased experiment with the participant. In the first phase, you get him to lift up a 2.3 kg (5 lb) weight off a table with his left hand. In the second phase, you get him to do 20 burpees, taking his heart rate to 150/min. In the third phase, you electrically stimulate his gastrocnemius with a frequency of 50 Hz. You are interested in the tension and electrical activity of specific muscles as follows: Biceps in phase 1, cardiac muscle in phase 2, and gastrocnemius in phase 3. What would you expect to be happening in the phases and the respective muscles of interest?

options.opa: Recruitment of small motor units at the start of experiments 1 and 2
options.opb: Increase of tension in experiments 2 and 3, with the same underlying mechanism
options.opc: Recruitment of large motor units followed by small motor units in experiment 1
options.opd: Fused tetanic contraction at the end of all three experiments
options.ope: Increase of tension in all phases

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Recruitment of small motor units at the start of experiments 1 and 2 -> Increase of tension in experiments 2 and 3, with the same underlying mechanism -> Increase of tension in all phases -> 80%

CHAIN: Recruitment of large motor units followed by small motor units in experiment 1 -> Increase of tension in experiments 2 and 3, with the same underlying mechanism -> Increase of tension in all phases -> 75%
analysis: In phase 1, lifting a weight would initially recruit small motor units for fine control, followed by larger motor units for more force. In phase 2, the cardiac muscle would increase tension due to increased heart rate, likely through increased calcium influx. In phase 3, electrical stimulation of the gastrocnemius would lead to fused tetanic contractions at higher frequencies. Therefore, the most likely scenario is an increase of tension in all phases, with different underlying mechanisms.
